clue.text: Saw professional introducing part of speech

parts.note: pro is the short form of professional
a verb is one of the parts of speech, like noun or adjective

explanation.surface: A professional brings in a part of speech, as in a grammar lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past tense; it is the noun meaning an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, a synonym.

clue.text: She opened the fateful box a pardon is out of order

indicators.note: something out of order is jumbled, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pardon is refused for the woman who released the world's troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out of order' rearranges A PARDON.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the first woman opened a jar or box releasing all evils into the world.

clue.text: No longer valid without an appointment?

definitions.meaning: expired, like an old ticket or passport
read literally, lacking a date or engagement

explanation.surface: Something expired, or someone who has no engagement booked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something expired has passed its date; someone with no date is literally without one.

clue.text: In the thick of the battle he stressed a moral principle

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the words that follow, the thick

explanation.surface: In the heat of combat a soldier insisted on a moral rule.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer lies within 'thE THICk'; the rest of the surface, 'of the battle he stressed', is padding for the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral principle or code of conduct guiding behaviour.

clue.text: Stop Carol adding a note in Venetian boat song

parts.note: to bar is to stop or block
taken as written
E is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: A singer named Carol is stopped from adding a note to a gondola song.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a song traditionally sung by Venetian gondoliers.

clue.text: Withdraw support? Impossible!

parts.note: to back is to support
out as in 'that's out', not possible

explanation.surface: Someone asked to withdraw support exclaims that it cannot be done.
explanation.definitionFit: To back out is to withdraw from an agreement, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Unreal wet spongy ground gets on top of us

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on top of another means it comes first

parts.note: a bog is soft wet ground
taken as written

explanation.surface: Damp marshy terrain gets us down, unreally so.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogus means fake or sham, a synonym of unreal.

clue.text: Cold tart, a lot of tea and baked dessert

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
tart is slang for a promiscuous woman, a harlot

indicators.note: a lot of a word means most of it, so the last letter of tea is dropped

explanation.surface: A menu of cold tart, plenty of tea and a baked pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a pastry, fitting the dessert menu, but it is HARLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte is a baked pudding of fruit in a bread or sponge casing.

clue.text: Australia has an individual layer of protection

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: Australia has a single protective layer over it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ozone hole was famously over Australia and Antarctica, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The ozone layer shields the earth from ultraviolet radiation.

clue.text: The control legally is in that place

parts.note: taken as written
to rein is to control, or a rein is a means of control

explanation.surface: A law clause states that control rests in a particular place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legally' marks the word as legal language; it and 'is' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is formal or legal language for in that place or thing.

clue.text: Nick is negative about Henry

parts.note: not expresses a negative
C stands for circa, about
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Nick is pessimistic about a man called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name to go with Henry; it is a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small cut or groove, a synonym.

clue.text: Equip graduate to take part in long, complex procedure

parts.note: to rig is to equip, as with a ship
an MA is a Master of Arts graduate
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: Kitting out a graduate for a role is a tiresome business.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a lengthy, complicated and tedious process.

clue.text: Functionaries are poor here in French half of Alsace

parts.note: off as in an off day, poor in quality
ici is French for here

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word gives its first three letters

explanation.surface: Bureaucrats in French Alsace are badly off.
explanation.definitionFit: Officials are functionaries holding public office.

clue.text: Tell fibs for example about Belgian place

parts.note: to lie is to tell fibs

indicators.note: about signals the abbreviation that follows is turned round

explanation.surface: Someone tells lies, say, about a town in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Liège is a city in eastern Belgium.

clue.text: Embarrass sailor with a request for silence

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
sh is said to ask for quiet

explanation.surface: A sailor shushing someone causes embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to make someone feel ashamed or disconcerted.

clue.text: Bob's one hot air technique

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
taken as written
a style is a manner or technique

explanation.surface: Bob boasts a technique using hot air, like a hairdryer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is a short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short haircut, so it is one example of a cut.

clue.text: Passed by other drivers with deliveries to convey north

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six deliveries
to take is to convey or carry

explanation.surface: A delivery van heading north is passed by other vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overtaken is to be passed by vehicles moving faster.

clue.text: Old time traveller beginning to tease outgoing person

parts.note: ex means former
a rover wanders far

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A former time-traveller starts teasing a sociable type.
explanation.definitionFit: An extrovert is a sociable, outgoing person.

clue.text: Stops taking sharp action to get motorcycle going

parts.note: to kick a habit is to stop it
tart means sharp in taste

explanation.surface: Someone stops and takes sharp action to start a motorbike.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick-start is the pedal action that starts a motorcycle engine.

clue.text: Head of state is living quietly after suffering reverse

indicators.note: the clue's order of living then quietly is reversed, so quietly comes first

parts.note: p is piano, quietly in music
resident means living in a place

explanation.surface: A head of state lives quietly after a political setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after suffering reverse' swaps the order of the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the elected head of a republic.

clue.text: Type of exercise to get reporters out of bed?

parts.note: the press is reporters collectively
up means risen from bed

explanation.surface: An exercise routine to rouse journalists in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up is a floor exercise pushing the body up with the arms.

clue.text: Old church and laity initially do very well

parts.note: ex means former
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter

explanation.surface: An ex-churchman and the laity at first perform brilliantly.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to be outstandingly good at something.

clue.text: New arrival's clothing etc held up still at the centre

indicators.note: at the centre means placed in the middle of the reversed piece
in a down clue held up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: et al is Latin for and others, etc
yet means still

explanation.surface: Baby clothes and the like are kept upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns ET AL into LATE; 'at the centre' puts YET in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is a set of clothing for a newborn baby.

clue.text: Tests maximum rotation between two points

indicators.note: between means placed inside the two compass points

parts.note: E and S are two compass points
max is short for maximum

explanation.surface: Engineers test maximum spin between two fixed points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' suggests a scoring or geometry sense, but here it means compass points; 'rotation' signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: Exams are tests of knowledge.

clue.text: Alabama and Ohio have a way of saying hello

parts.note: AL is the postal code of Alabama
OH is the postal code of Ohio

explanation.surface: Two American states share a way of greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The greeting is Hawaiian, another US state, which fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloha is a Hawaiian greeting used for hello and goodbye.

clue.text: Your lot is getting drunk in a very disorderly manner

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Your group is getting drunk and behaving rowdily.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotously means wildly and unrestrainedly, a synonym.

clue.text: Money can be a beast in Asia and Africa

definitions.text: a beast in Asia and Africa
definitions.meaning: a large horned animal of both continents

explanation.surface: Money can be found in a wild beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old slang for money and short for rhinoceros.

clue.text: Exist on nothing but fruit

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to live is to exist

explanation.surface: Someone survives on nothing except fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An olive is the small oily fruit of the olive tree.

clue.text: Socialist policy to contain Conservative plot

indicators.note: to contain means to hold the next piece inside

parts.note: S abbreviates socialist
a party line is its policy
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A socialist policy meant to restrain a Tory scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyline is the plot of a novel or film.

clue.text: In Italy, siesta would be inappropriate

indicators.note: in means the following piece is placed inside Italy

parts.note: IT is the international code for Italy
a siesta is an afternoon nap

explanation.surface: In Italy, an afternoon nap would be out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable, a synonym of inappropriate.

clue.text: Pretend treatment could contain station smell

parts.note: a station is a position or place
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A fake remedy could contain the smell of a railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill or sham medical treatment.

clue.text: Plays the field of operations, military and civil

definitions.text: field of operations, military and civil
definitions.meaning: a war zone, and also a hospital operating room

explanation.surface: Plays and the scene of military and surgical operations.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre is drama, a theatre of war, and an operating theatre.
